newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Meyer--oil prices may damp inflation in '97.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Meyer--oil prices may damp inflation in '97.

text.p: Federal Reserve Gov. Laurence Meyer on Wednesday said oil prices could decline in coming months, a situation that would help the inflation outlook.
"In terms of energy prices, they continue to be elevated, and they have added considerably to inflation over 1996," Meyer said in an interview with the Nightly Business Report on PBS television.

"My own guess is that we'll see some decline oil prices in particular over the course of the next several months, that energy will be a factor that acutally is moderating rather than feeding inflation over 1997," Meyer said.
He added, however, that there was some uncertainty in the oil price forecast, given the sharp increase and the extent to which it has lasted.
Asked whether he was concerned that fundamentals in the stock market might pose a risk to the economy, Meyer replied, "This is not one of the factors I am most concerned with now."

Asked to elaborate on his recent comment describing the economy as being at the "top of the mountain" and that all roads lead down from there, Meyer replied that what he meant was that, with the economy running so well, there are risks that could change.

"We're close to capacity, maybe at full employment, we're growing at trend -- we're growing at about the rate that productive capacity will allow, and inflation looks very favorable," he said. "In that environment, lower growth or higher growth become risk factors in the economy."
Meyer was also asked for his outlook for growth, given data suggesting a pickup in activity toward the end of last year.
"If you look at growth over the last year, it has bounced around quite a bit ... but I'd say going forward I'd expect to see growth closer to trend."
